newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money continue rise on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money continue rise on rate hike.

text.p: *Central Bank lifts overnight borrowing to 20 from 13 pct

Manila overnight money continued to rise on Friday to an average of 13.03125 from 12.03125 percent after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing by another one percentage point to 13 percent late on Thursday, traders said.
Traders said the rates would further rise on Monday to take into account the latest rate hike to 20 percent.
The Central Bank raised its key rate by 8.75 percentage points in two days to quell peso speculation.
The peso has been hit from the backlash of the problems of the Thai baht.
Done rates rose to 13.25 to 13.03125 percent, with volume down to 9.58 billion from 12.38 billion pesos.
The secondary market continued to have lacklustre trading.
"Banks were holding off on buying bills because of the possibility of another rate increase," a dealer said before the Central Bank eventually raised its rate to 20 percent.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave bids of 10.70/11.10 and offers of 10.60/11 percent for the three-month bills.
